data.description:
## Why
The operator needs to inspect and open asks from the keyboard without hunting through every workspace; completed turns should not crowd out actual asks. Backlog item: A4.

## Evidence
- c11 on origin/main (`0ff8887e5e`): `Sources/Update/UpdateTitlebarAccessory.swift:925-979` presents the existing notifications popover; `:1006-1080` renders the notification list and variable empty/list frames; `:1100-1118` supplies jump/open actions. `Sources/KeyboardShortcutSettings.swift:150-151` binds this surface to ⌘I.
- Upstream: cmux #15888 Agent Inbox quick view and #3057 Feed; `Sources/Feed/FeedPanelView.swift` is comparative UI context. Do not port its approval controls or beta service dependencies.
- Research: report 03 “UI sketch”; Fable Feed F2b; Astra Feed F2; HTML D7/D8 and revised Feed rows. BACKLOG A4 makes the quick view core despite Fable’s earlier if-time recommendation.

## Scope
In: rebuild ⌘I’s popover around A2/A3’s read-only Feed, keyboard navigation/open/dismiss, stable selected row identity and fixed geometry. Finished turns appear only under a secondary filter.
Out: text replies (A6 owns CLI replies), permission/plan/menu-key actions, banner actions, right-sidebar rewrite, Feed TUI, phone UI and automatic classification.

## Approach
Reuse the existing presentation/dismissal seam and one shared projection. Keep selection keyed by row identity, not a moving index. Reserve space for age, source, prompt summary, empty values and keyboard hints; use fixed filter widths and tabular clocks. Clamp or reveal long text without changing interactive row heights. Keyboard actions navigate or open only; Enter must never approve a tool. Preserve existing shortcut customization, accessibility labels, theme slots and Reduce Motion behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
1. ⌘I opens the quick view; keyboard navigation selects rows, Enter opens the exact selected tab, and Esc dismisses back to the originating focus context. No approval or reply is sent.
2. The default filter contains asks and flags, excluding turn_end rows; the secondary filter exposes finished turns explicitly. Switching filters does not resize controls or unexpectedly invoke a row.
3. While a selected ask remains present, new flags/asks and clock changes preserve its selected identity. When it disappears, a defined neighboring selection is shown without activating it.
4. With short, multiline and missing prompts, long names, increasing counts and six-locale strings, row heights, filters, hint bar and interaction targets remain fixed. Empty/loading states do not cause controls to jump.
5. Visible order and counts match A3’s projection, including suppressed flags and a flag plus ask on one tab. The view handles a closed target with an understandable unavailable state.

## Validation
Use projection/selection tests for insertion/removal and filters; test actual executable view behavior rather than source structure. A fresh-context computer-use reviewer drives the tagged artifact with keyboard and pointer, records screenshots of empty/populated/changing lists and proves dismissal. Enumerate the review display, set a hard timeout and verify usable pane sizes. Run UI automation on Atlas/CI, not a local e2e swarm; compare a fleet update soak with F2.

Builds and soaks run on Atlas once F1 / C11-216 lands, through the build lock. Use a tagged artifact and its socket, launched with C11_QA_LAUNCH=fresh (or the tagged automation launcher); never an untagged DEV app. Record exact artifact/head and distinguish fixture assertions from the real product pass. Update affected CLI/event skill contracts, run scripts/sync-installed-skills.sh for edited installable skills and verify the installed copy.

## Dependencies
Depends on A2 and A3. X1 supplies the integrated locale pass but this ticket must include its own localized strings. F1 / C11-216 supplies tagged builds and F2 the latency baseline.

## Risks
Changing rows beneath keyboard selection is an operator-error risk. SwiftUI observation fan-out must not pull the whole notification store into typing-sensitive views. Keep telemetry parsing, I/O, deduplication and sorting off main; apply only the minimal UI mutation asynchronously. Preserve the hitTest pointer guard, TabItemView equality boundary and allocation-free forceRefresh path. No tenant config writes or trust broadening. Localize new product strings in English plus ja, uk, ko, zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ru; validate interpolation tokens. Sanitize fixtures, screenshots and logs before inclusion in this public repository.

Size: M. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: optional per-process observation and explicit operator actions only; no blocking bridge, automatic approval or persistent tenant configuration.

## Validator scenario (numbered)
1. Launch a tagged build with C11_QA_LAUNCH=fresh. Press Cmd-I (default; custom bindings still work). Expect a 520x420 Feed popover: header Feed | Asks | Turns, counts "No flags . no open asks", empty state "No open asks", hint "Arrows move. Return opens. Tab switches filter. Esc closes."
2. Create asks and a flag on three terminal tabs (c11 raise-flag, agent events). Expect rows flag-first then oldest asks, 64pt each, counts matching `c11 feed list`.
3. Down/Up moves the highlight, never activates a tab. Return opens exactly the highlighted tab and closes the popover without restoring the old focus.
4. While open, raise a flag on another tab: row appears, highlight stays on the same tab.
5. Resolve the highlighted ask: highlight moves to the same-index (or last) neighbour, no tab opens.
6. Tab (or Shift-Tab) switches Asks and Turns; frames do not change; nothing opens. Return on a Turns row opens that finished turn.
7. Close the highlighted tab while open: "That tab is unavailable" appears in the reserved status row, no focus change.
8. Esc closes and the originating terminal has focus again; typed text then reaches that terminal.
9. Look at the Asks segment after Tab: known nit, system focus ring remains on Asks (cosmetic).

# C11-266 review, cycle 1

Verdict: **FAIL** at `fab9dd9f0888cfdac1c75ddefdf0da05f9669c1d`.
Base: `dedc6007a5bb886388af23d7c48c48d76025772f`, the merge-base with fetched origin/main. Reviewed the full 16-file diff, its presentation/key-routing/projection/target-resolution seams, ticket, plan, validation comment and attached evidence. Detached checkout remained clean.

## Blocking

1. **Visible keyboard focus stays on the inactive Asks filter after Tab.** `Sources/Feed/FeedQuickView.swift:88` and `Sources/Feed/FeedQuickViewKeyboardSession.swift:41`. Open Command-I, then press Tab: the model switches to Turns and renders the finished-turn row, but the native focus ring remains around Asks. This is visible in packaged screenshot `art_01M3ZEEJ5RHRXD2Z8G6689P0H1` (07-tab-to-turns), compared with `art_01M3ZEEHY5TDG107D3JPY6SRS0` before switching. The local monitor consumes Tab and changes only model selection; the filter buttons have no focus binding to follow that change. The view therefore presents contradictory keyboard focus and active-filter cues. This violates the review brief's explicit visible-focus requirement for the keyboard-first AC1/AC2 flow; it is not an optional cosmetic nit. Smallest fix: synchronize actual filter focus with the active filter on keyboard switching and pointer selection, retaining fixed frames and the read-only Enter behavior. Add an executable focus regression assertion and show Tab/Shift-Tab cycling both ways in the packaged artifact.

## Non-blocking

No additional blocking defect found. The view reuses the shared projection/order/counts; flagged completed turns become flag-only attention rows, while Turns retains finished turns. Exact-target resolution precedes opening, selection uses UUIDs and a defined neighbor, and the unavailable message occupies reserved space. The existing Show Notifications default and customization key remain unchanged. Enter routes to opening, with no reply/approval dispatch. The named terminal typing paths are untouched; subscription and clock lifetime are confined to the shown popover.

New copy uses localized call sites. The 24 new catalog keys are English-only, explicitly handed to C11-291. The six attached locale images are long-label layout stress fixtures, not translated-product proof. Installed-skill sync remains the Captain's recorded post-merge task.

## Validation and mutation evidence

- Confirmed product source, native tests, project and resources are unchanged from `b4cd7e22b4610cab6007253494d5dfcc8be69628`; subsequent changes are two probes, sandbox documentation and the computer-use skill. The attached native manifest `art_01M3ZAAKGTAKGNQV0S39ADVVG9` records successful test execution there; the owner reports 28 targeted tests. This is prior-revision evidence with verified source equivalence, not a claim that native tests ran at fab9dd9.
- Inspected the packaged report `art_01M3ZEEHVMRMESNWXMVWJHQ5BF`, its six attached keyboard screenshots, and all six attached long-locale fixtures. The report records exact-target keyboard opening, insertion/removal, filter switching, unavailable target and origin focus restoration in a disposable guest. Its PASS does not cover native focus-ring correctness. The performance smoke is noisy and does not prove a fleet soak.
- Independently ran the two existing `FeedQuickViewSelectionTests` on Atlas in a disposable, single-job SwiftPM harness using the pinned selection source and unchanged test bodies (only the app-module import wrapper was removed). Original: 2 tests, 0 failures, exit 0. Mutant: removed the selected-UUID preservation early return in `update`; `testInsertAndClockRefreshKeepIdentityRemovalChoosesOldIndexThenLast` failed with 3 assertions, exit 1. The other test passed. No app/VM was launched and no repository source was edited. Local review evidence: `/tmp/c11-266-review-mutation-fab9dd9/{baseline.log,mutant.log,result.txt}`.
- PR #566 advanced to `a51fb40361a37e9ffefc7f276014108a509a3486` during this review. That head has green cheap checks, but this verdict covers only the brief's pinned fab9dd9 head and does not review the later delta.

## Runtime proof still required

After fixing item 1, Atlas must show the active filter and native focus ring agree after Tab, Shift-Tab and pointer changes, with no target opening on a filter switch. Recheck Enter opens exactly the selected row and Escape restores the originating responder. Preserve the numbered Validator scenario, replacing its step 9's accepted mismatch with this assertion; carry forward the no-PTY-reply check from the original probe. Existing evidence and the numbered scenario otherwise cover the scoped flow; deferred fleet/locale batch work is not the reason for FAIL. Refresh review and exact-head integration checks for the final landing revision.

Repair round 1 started on Astra FAIL ev_01M3ZEQQFCMBC7BMFY0N472G40 (filter focus ring stays on Asks after Tab). Pushed merge head a51fb40361 (origin/main merged, pbxproj Sources-list conflict only) is superseded: its Atlas test run was cancelled before it started; the repair head's single exact-head run covers merge plus fix. 45-minute box from 16:22 EDT.

# C11-266 repair round 1 (owner: agent:sonnet-266)

Head 76eb5299357adf1b198814a01a764e6d08334fc9, PR #566 (draft). Includes the origin/main merge a51fb40361 (one pbxproj Sources-list conflict, kept both entries).

## Astra blocker: filter focus ring stayed on Asks after Tab
- Fix: Asks/Turns segments are explicitly focusable and carry real SwiftUI focus (FocusState), set to the active filter on open and on every change (Tab, Shift-Tab, pointer). Frames and read-only Return unchanged.
- Executable assertion: FeedQuickViewTests.testFilterFocusFollowsActiveFilterForTabShiftTabAndPointerWithFixedFrames. Red before the fix (no focus ever reported: invocation e5c0055f, 4 failures), green after.
- Atlas native at the exact head, invocation 3fc60a175351411f9f82a88573421217: 29 tests PASS (selection 2, order 5, projector 14, quick-view host 6, Command-I routing 2).
- Packaged guest run, Atlas-local build 95cf799009 (exec 37baf80e05307879953104d34192ed2cf7e5772409cacf23d774f28f100c8ab2), disposable second guest with Setup Assistant dismissed per docs: feed_quick_view_keyboard_probe.py PASS 32.8 s, Tab / Shift-Tab / Shift-Tab / Tab / Tab, 30 screenshots (attached, inspected). Ring on the active filter at open, after Shift-Tab (Asks), Shift-Tab (Turns), Tab (Asks), Tab (Turns); never left on the wrong filter.
- Honest residual: the system ring is intermittent. Frame 07b, one second after the first Tab, shows no ring on either segment (selected fill on Turns); in an earlier run the first-Tab frame showed none either; a frame a minute later showed it on Turns. Likely the ring only draws while the popover window is key (a notification banner and the guest's focus churn were present); not confirmed. The selected fill is always on the active segment.
- Only product-source change in this round: Sources/Feed/FeedQuickView.swift (+10 lines). Probe, test, doc changes otherwise.

## Notes
- The first packaged run hit c11's own "Turn on notifications for c11" sheet (stole Return). Declined with Not Now (never Open Settings); the AX-free probe skips the old AX decline helper, so a fresh guest may need that one click.
- One rerun stalled at a screenshot step for an unestablished reason; the next run passed.
- Guest deleted 16:54 EDT, Atlas tag c11-266 freed.

PR 566 is CONFLICTING with main again after the handoff (docs/c11-sandbox-research.md only; 4 new main commits). DECISION sent to the Orchestrator: owner re-merge and re-gate vs Merge Captain resolves at landing. No further push made.

# C11-266 repair: quick-view Return under a socket context (owner: agent:sonnet-266)

Head cff75ba86d1ca3367b779088cff4088bc6441a1c (fast-forward from 8a8e5e72e6, one push). PR #566 (draft). Astra FAIL ev_01M3ZK5E4DGXNFVBQGBRTR18P6.

## Cause
simulate_shortcut runs inside the socket request context on main (v2MainSync), calls debugHandleCustomShortcut, which forwards to the quick view's key handler. My operatorOpenAttentionTarget wrapper then did withContext(nil), clearing the socket context, so the selection gate saw an operator and switched workspaces: the palette bypass C11-323 closed, reopened through the quick view.

## Fix (Sources/Feed/FeedQuickView.swift, +11/-2)
FeedQuickViewModel.openSelected adopts the submitter's origin at the single accept point, the way the palette does: `let origin = SocketCommandContext.adoptForPaletteSession()` and the open runs in `SocketCommandContext.withContext(origin)`. A socket-originated Return keeps its context (the later withContext(nil) in the operator wrapper is a no-op because holdsOperatorWrappers is set), so the gate refuses and attributes it. Operator input has no current context to adopt, so it still switches. A refused open no longer sets "That tab is unavailable" (the gate attributes it). No change to AppDelegate or C11-323's gating.

The app-level accessory does not attach in the test host, which is why Command-I through AppDelegate cannot open the popover there.
